title: Mandatos — Practice
description: Authored B1 practice set for commands: affirmative tú forms and the eight irregulars, negative tú commands via the subjunctive, pronoun attachment (dámelo / no me lo des), and polite usted forms.

lessons.summary: Affirmative tú commands look like the él/ella present: habla, come, abre — 'Habla más despacio', 'Abre la boquita'. Eight verbs go rogue and are worth knowing cold: pon (poner), ten (tener), ven (venir), sal (salir), haz (hacer), di (decir), ve (ir), sé (ser) — 'Ven acá', 'Ten cuidado', 'Dame la mano' (da + me). NEGATIVE tú commands switch to the present subjunctive: no hables, no comas, no toques, no vayas — never «no habla». Pronouns follow a strict geography: they ATTACH to the end of an affirmative command (dámelo, siéntate, lávate las manos — often adding an accent to keep the stress) but go BEFORE a negative one (no me lo des, no te levantes). Usted commands use the subjunctive in both directions: hable / no hable, pase / no pase — the polite register for the doctor's office or a stranger. Around the house with a toddler this is bread and butter: ven, dame, mira, ten cuidado, no toques, siéntate.

examples.spanish: Siéntate, que ya llega la comida.

items.prompt: ¡___ acá, que te pongo los zapatos!
items.promptEnglish: Come here, let me put your shoes on!
items.explanation: Venir has the irregular tú command ven. Vienes just states that you're coming; venga is the usted form.

items.prompt: ___ cuidado con el escalón. (tener, mandato tú)
items.explanation: Tener → ten, one of the eight irregular tú commands.
Negative tú commands use the subjunctive: no toques. «No toca» is the classic slip.

items.prompt: ___ la boquita, que viene el avión. (abrir, mandato tú)
items.promptEnglish: Open wide, here comes the aeroplane.
items.explanation: Regular affirmative tú command = the él/ella present form: abre.

items.prompt: Eso no es un juguete — ___, por favor.
items.promptEnglish: That's not a toy — give it to me, please.
items.explanation: Pronouns attach to the end of an affirmative command, written as one word with an accent: dá-me-lo.

items.prompt: Está sucio — no ___ a la boca.
items.promptEnglish: It's dirty — don't put it in your mouth.
items.explanation: With a NEGATIVE command the pronouns go before the verb, in te-lo order: no te lo lleves.

items.prompt: ___ en la sillita, que vamos a comer. (sentarse, mandato tú)
items.promptEnglish: Sit in your high chair, we're going to eat.
items.explanation: Reflexive pronoun attaches: sienta + te → siéntate, with an accent to keep the stress on -sién-.

items.prompt: ___ como papá: sopla la sopa primero.
items.promptEnglish: Do like daddy: blow on the soup first.
items.explanation: Hacer → haz in the tú command. Hace is just the present; haga is usted.

items.promptEnglish: Don't cry, it's OK, it's over.
items.explanation: Negative tú command → subjunctive: no llores.

items.prompt: ___ qué te duele. (decir + me, mandato tú)
items.explanation: Decir → di, plus the attached pronoun: dime.

items.prompt: En la sala de espera: «___ por aquí, señora.»
items.promptEnglish: In the waiting room: "Come through this way, madam."
items.explanation: Usted commands use the subjunctive form: pase. Pasa would be the informal tú command.

items.prompt: Ya es tarde — ___ a la cama.
items.promptEnglish: It's late now — off to bed.
items.explanation: Ir(se) → ve + te attached: vete. (Ve alone is also the command for ir — and, confusingly, for ver.)

items.prompt: ___ las manos antes de comer. (lavarse, mandato tú)
items.explanation: Reflexive attaches to the affirmative command: lava + te → lávate. Note it's las manos, not «tus manos».
Negative tú command = no + subjunctive: no corras. The bare present or infinitive don't make commands here.
